To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RNA hairpin assemblies can be used for amplification of target nucleic acids and for computation.
we have developed a non enzymatic, cotranscriptional RNA amplification reaction and demonstrated its use in the end point and quantitative detection of DNA targets.
we have demonstrated that RNA can be used to implement nucleic acid circuits that can perform amplification reactions and computations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the engineering of RNA circuits and the application of these circuits in diagnostics and synthetic biotechnology.
the development and application of non-enzymatic RNA circuitry.
the development of RNA-based circuits that can be used for reagent production, signal transduction, and computation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNA circuits can operate in the same manner as DNA circuits, and that RNA circuits can be used in the same way as DNA circuits.

the RNA circuitry is a powerful and versatile tool for the detection and quantification of DNA targets, which can be used as a stand-alone tool for the detection of DNA targets or in combination with other DNA amplification methods.
RNA circuits are a powerful alternative to DNA circuits for a wide variety of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design principles of DNA circuits can be readily translated to RNA and that the RNA circuits can be used to implement complex signal transduction and computation.
RNA can be readily engineered into circuits that are capable of performing non-enzymatic amplification reactions.
the design and application of cotrascriptional non enzymic RNA circuits and signal processing elements are now possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA could provide an attractive alternative to DNA for nucleic acid circuits that could be used in diagnostics, in cells, and for in vivo imaging.
the use of RNA as a substrate for the implementation of non-enzymatic nucleic acid circuits is possible, practical and can be applied to the design of novel diagnostic tools.
RNA could be a powerful new tool for nucleic acid circuit engineering and that the design principles for DNA circuits could readily be translated to engineering RNA circuit designs.
